title: Quitting in Little Rock after a lynching
summary: Roy quit the show after arriving in Little Rock a week after a man was lynched, and was threatened by a policeman.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: No. It's just... That was in 1927, right? That was the year they hung that guy, drug him down on the main street, the main Black neighborhood, you know, picked him up and burned him there.

Yeah! I come there the week after that happened. And I was quitting. And I asked a policeman... Well, you see, I used to speak different than I do now, that Pennsylvania thing. "You did?" I mean, that Pennsylvania stuff. And this damn policeman... I asked him where I could get an express truck to haul my stuff into town. Boy, he went off. He said, "Oo-ooh. You're up there from where the niggers cuss the Whitefolks, eh?" I said... I'd learned by now. I said, "No-suh." "Do you know where you're at?" I said, "Yes-suh." He said, "If I catch you out after twelve o'clock, I'm gonna lock you up." Heh-heh.
